prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which designed small molecules, from bifunctional PROTACs to cereblon-dependent molecular glues, direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to chosen proteins

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: one prize part, B023, to Crews, Deshaies and Handa. Targeted protein degradation is a new chemical modality in which a designed molecule converts occupancy-driven pharmacology into event-driven removal of a chosen protein by the ubiquitin-proteasome system. The mechanism is chemically explicit (ternary-complex cooperativity, linker and ligase-ligand design, the cereblon degron) and independent groups have confirmed it for two decades. Round 1 showed six of eight members preferring B023 on the same scientific grounds, but I rest my position on the chemistry and not on that count. Crews and Deshaies established the PROTAC concept and first demonstrations. Handa's identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide explains why lenalidomide and pomalidomide, which are approved drugs, work, and so ties the glue strand to the same induced-proximity logic. A single citation naming induced proximity to the ubiquitin-proteasome system can honestly cover both strands, because the shared principle is the discovery and the two histories are two routes to it. I have widened the round-1 citation to name PROTACs and cereblon-dependent glues explicitly, so that it does not claim more than the three names support.
statement.case_against: No bifunctional degrader is approved, so the clinical payoff of the PROTAC half is still forward-looking, and the approved glue-class drugs validate cereblon biology more than they validate designed bifunctionals. A three-person limit omits Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure), Sakamoto (first PROTAC with Crews and Deshaies), Gray, and Ito and Kim (cereblon), and whichever three are chosen one strand will look under-credited. The combined citation may also read as two discoveries joined for convenience. If the committee judges maturity strictly, B002 is cleaner in attribution and more settled, even though it extends a field honoured in 2010.

responses.point: Aqvist keeps B023 first but names Ciulli as the third laureate, arguing that VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures turned the PROTAC concept into a general, drug-like platform, and that cereblon is a target-identification result in one drug class.
responses.response: This is the strongest argument for Ciulli and I have weighed it again. I still come down for Handa, for a reason about the citation. Without Handa the citation would be a PROTAC-only citation and would leave out the cereblon mechanism, which explains how an approved drug class works and is where the induced-proximity logic was first realised in humans. Ciulli's work generalised a platform whose concept Crews and Deshaies already carry, so it strengthens the case without being the point where the idea originated. I disagree with calling cereblon only a target-identification result in one class, because it is also the molecular basis for neosubstrate degradation. I hold this as a close call and I would vote for Ciulli's configuration if the committee narrowed the citation to PROTACs only; that would change the logic, and I would then ask whether B023 is mature enough in that narrower form.

responses.point: Somfai prefers B002 (Buchwald and Hartwig), calls it overdue and cleanly attributed, and argues that the 2010 prize covered C-C bond formation and does not preclude C-N coupling.
responses.response: I accept that C-N coupling is a distinct bond construction and that the 2010 prize does not formally exclude it, and I accept your point that attribution to two groups is cleaner than anything B023 offers. My difference is about what a prize now should say. B002 would reward a late, well-settled chapter of a recognised field, while B023 recognises a mechanism that is established and has become a field in its own right. Your own case against B002 says that timing for degradation could be perfectly good in the next few years, and I think the mechanistic evidence already supports it now. I would not be unhappy with B002 as the committee's outcome, which is why it stays my first alternative, but I do not see that the absence of an approved bifunctional degrader should outweigh two decades of independent mechanistic confirmation.

responses.point: Zou holds B002 first because it is the only top candidate where both the discovery and the credit are settled, while acknowledging that B023 is conceptually fresher and that she may be underweighting novelty.
responses.response: Your note that you may be underweighting novelty is fair, and I think the real disagreement between us is how to weigh settled credit against conceptual reach. I agree the credit in B002 is cleaner, including the need to handle Kosugi in the wording. But a three-name cut in B023 does not leave the credit unsettled: Crews and Deshaies on the concept and Handa on the mechanism are each defensible, with the omissions being honest limits of the prize rule and not doubts about the science. I would ask whether any B023 configuration would move you, since the chair's summary notes you could name an acceptable one, and I would welcome your view on whether Handa or Ciulli would be easier to accept.

responses.point: Sparr moved to B023 and prefers Handa to Ciulli in the third seat, because cereblon is a separate mechanistic discovery explaining an existing drug, while Ciulli refines a platform whose concept Crews and Deshaies had already established.
responses.response: I agree with your reasoning and it is close to mine. Where I would add a caution is that your argument works only if the citation names the cereblon mechanism, because otherwise Handa's inclusion looks unexplained to outsiders. That is why I have written the cereblon-dependent glues into the citation. I also note your remaining worry that the absence of an approved degrader makes some of the impact forward-looking. I share it, and I regard it as a ranking factor against B002 and not as disqualifying, given that the glue half is already in clinical use.

responses.point: Chabes argues that Handa's cereblon work is a mechanistic discovery that explains why a long-used drug works, and that the PROTAC and glue halves cannot be separated.
responses.response: I agree that the clinical use of thalidomide-class drugs is a real validation for the glue half, and I use it in my own case. I would not go as far as saying the halves cannot be separated, because their histories differ and a reader could argue for two prizes. I think they can be held together as one discovery, induced proximity to the ubiquitin-proteasome system, but only if the citation says so openly and does not suggest that Handa invented PROTACs.

uncertainties: Whether the third laureate should be Handa or Ciulli; I judge it close and would accept Ciulli if the committee prefers a platform-focused citation.
Whether one citation can cover PROTACs and cereblon-dependent glues without implying a single origin, given that Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim are omitted.
Whether the absence of an approved bifunctional degrader makes recognition premature compared with B002.
Whether the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize should count against B002 in the committee's view.
My recollection of detailed priority claims is not independently verified.
statement.conflict_note: As chair I preside over the discussion and the vote counts like any other member's. My profile (Lund; nanophysics, thermoelectrics, molecular motors) shows no personal or institutional tie to any person in the shortlisted configurations. Somfai and Sparr are also at Lund, which is not a tie to any candidate. No conflict or recusal to disclose; this is unchanged from round 1.
